answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity itself: each agent must lock a refundable stake and build a public record of completed, peer-attested work before it can take paid jobs. A single honest agent climbs one terrace at a time, earning trust step by step, while an attacker flooding the market must fund a separate stake for every clone and wait out the same slow climb. The cost scales with each fake, like trying to dye an entire ocean violet one drop at a time: possible in theory, ruinous in practice, and easy for peers to spot when a hundred brand-new agents appear overnight.
